title: Introduction to Laboratory Chemistry - Chemistry - Laboratory Apparatus and Measurements
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following pieces of glassware is designed to contain a precise volume of liquid at a specific temperature, making it the ideal choice for preparing standard solutions?
questions.explain: A **volumetric flask** is calibrated to contain a precise volume of liquid when filled to the mark, making it the standard apparatus for preparing solutions of known concentration. Beakers and Erlenmeyer flasks are for mixing/holding, and graduated cylinders are less precise.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In a titration experiment, which apparatus is used to deliver a variable but precisely measured volume of the titrant?
questions.explain: A **buret** is a long, graduated glass tube with a stopcock at the bottom, specifically designed to dispense variable precise volumes of liquid (titrant) during a titration.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why is an Erlenmeyer flask preferred over a beaker for the analyte solution during an acid-base titration?
options: It measures volume more accurately than a beaker.
Its wide mouth allows for easier addition of the indicator.
Its narrow neck and sloped sides minimize splashing while swirling.
It is made of stronger glass that withstands heat better.
questions.explain: The conical shape (narrow neck and sloped sides) of an **Erlenmeyer flask** allows the user to swirl the solution vigorously to ensure mixing without splashing the liquid out, which is a risk with the wide mouth of a beaker.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which instrument would provide the most precise measurement for transferring exactly $25.00\ \text{mL}$ of a stock solution?
questions.explain: A **volumetric pipette** is calibrated to deliver a single, fixed volume with very high precision (often to $\pm 0.01\ \text{mL}$ or better), superior to graduated cylinders or beakers.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which apparatus is best suited for strongly heating a small amount of solid over a Bunsen burner flame?
questions.explain: A **crucible** is made of heat-resistant ceramic or metal and is designed to withstand the very high temperatures of direct flame heating, unlike watch glasses or volumetric glassware.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: When reading the volume of water in a glass graduated cylinder, how should the meniscus be observed to ensure an accurate reading?
options: Align the eye with the top of the liquid curve.
Align the eye with the bottom of the curved liquid surface.
Look down into the cylinder from above.
Look up at the cylinder from below.
questions.explain: For concave menisci (like water in glass), the correct technique is to position the eye level with the liquid surface and read the volume at the **bottom of the meniscus**.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: A student uses a buret marked in $0.1\ \text{mL}$ increments. Which of the following volume recordings represents the correct number of significant figures?
questions.explain: When recording a measurement, you estimate one digit beyond the smallest marking. Since the buret is marked every $0.1\ \text{mL}$, the reading should be estimated to the hundredths place ($0.01\ \text{mL}$), making **$20.15\ \text{mL}$** the correct format.
